newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-CRAWLEY HUNDRED GIVES ENGLAND UPPER HAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRAWLEY HUNDRED GIVES ENGLAND UPPER HAND.

text.p: A second test century from John Crawley gave England the upper hand against Zimbabwe for the first time on the fourth day of the opening test at Queen's Club on Saturday.
Crawley's 112, his second century in successive test matches, took England to 406 all out in their first innings and a potentially crucial lead of 30.

That performance was followed by the quick removal of the two openers Stuart Carlisle and Grant Flower in the Zimbabwe second innings. The English spinners then took a grip on the day as they collected another three wickets which meant that by stumps Zimbabwe had reached 107 for five, a lead of only 77.

Alan Mullally made the initial breakthrough when he had Carlisle caught at silly point by Mike Atherton for four and then, with the score still only on six, Darren Gough won a controversial lbw decision to remove Flower for a duck.
But there was no good fortune needed for the next three wickets as the spin duo of Robert Croft and Phil Tufnell got to work on a wearing pitch.
After a bright 51 run stand for the third wicket, Zimbabwe skipper Alistair Campbell was totally flummoxed by Croft's quicker arm ball and bowled for 29.

Slow-left armer Tufnell then got into the action as he had first innings centurion Andy Flower caught by Crawley at short-leg in his first over, the ball turning and bouncing out of the rough and flicking off the batsman's glove.

Then, in the penultimate over of the day, the Middlesex spinner took the crucial wicket of player/coach Dave Houghton whose grafting innings of 37 came to an end when he played across the spin and sent a leading edge out to Croft at mid-on.
Crawley's discipline had laid the foundation for the bowlers in the first two sessions as he added 112 to the century he made in his last test against Pakistan at the Oval in August.

Resuming at 306 for four Crawley lost his overnight partner Nasser Hussain after a quiet first hour when the England vice-captain, pulling Heath Streak for what seemed a certain six, was brilliantly caught one handed on the boundary by Bryan Strang.

Hussain had added just 12 to his overnight 101 and his 113 came from 278 balls with 14 boundaries. His dismissal also meant the end of a 148-run partnership for the fifth wicket with Crawley and resulted in the exposure of England's long tail.

When four wickets fell for the addition of just 25 runs, Zimbabwe looked likely to take the first innings lead but, in partnership with Mullally and Tufnell, Crawley put the innings back on track as the last two wickets added 53 important runs.

Crawley, who went to his century in spectacular fashion when he pulled a short ball from Streak for six, was finally the last man out, caught behind off the leg-spin of Paul Strang in an innings which lasted 297 balls and included nine fours and a six.
The deserving Strang bowled 58.4 overs and finished with five for 123.
